title: Clover at The Parks

text:
I’ve lived at Clover at the Parks for almost three years, since the community was newly built, and my experience has only gotten better over time. Since Greystar took over management, living here has been wonderful.

A special thank you to Chez the leasing manager, who has been incredibly responsive, professional, and helpful whenever I’ve needed assistance. As a newlywed preparing to welcome our baby, my housing needs changed, and Chez made the transfer process to a more accommodating unit smooth and stress-free.

The property is well maintained, the staff is attentive, and management truly cares about residents. I’m grateful to call Clover at the Parks home and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for a great place to live in NW DC.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Maya J
text:
Do NOT move here. The only reason I gave 1 star is because there's no option to give 0 and it is a nice location with close proximity to Whole Foods and Starbucks.

My relative lives here and has lived here for about a year. They do not answer the phone. They do not answer emails. There is rarely anyone available in the leasing office. God forbid anything happens to your unit, you will most likely not hear from anyone for days.

My relative had a lease with them. They called and asked if my relative wanted to move out well before the lease end date. My relative said no and opted to keep the lease end date as is. In response, the complex said my relative did not have a choice and would need to move out of the unit because the complex wanted the unit back. Keep in mind, there was no just cause as my relative has never been late paying rent, hasn't caused any destruction to anything on the property, and hasn't caused any disturbance to fellow neighbors or staff.

In all, I wouldn't bother with these people. Extremely unprofessional. Poor communication. Disrespectful staff, if you can even find them. Don't even bother. It's not worth the stress.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Jordan M
text:
There have been ongoing issues with extremely loud music coming from this property, often lasting for hours at a time. This has been a recurring problem.

The noise levels are so disruptive to nearby residents and the surrounding community, including families with children who need to sleep and get to school in the morning, as well as pets in the area who may be sensitive to loud, constant noise. It also affects professionals who need to get adequate rest before work and neighbors who are unable to fully enjoy their days off due to the ongoing disruption.

This is especially frustrating considering that the nearby marketplace events with music are generally much quieter and more reasonable in comparison. The contrast highlights how excessive the volume from this building can be.

This issue impacts not only their community, but two other residential buildings and nearby businesses as well. There seems to be little consideration for how far the noise travels or how disruptive it is to others living and working in the area.

Management needs to take this issue seriously and implement proper measures to ensure noise is controlled. Community neighbors feel terrible for those who actually reside in the building. May this review serve as validation to those impacted.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: 3_noch Music
text:
I’ve lived here long enough to see the decline firsthand, and it’s honestly disappointing. Ever since the management switch, things have gone downhill fast. Communication is poor, responses to maintenance requests are slow (if they come at all), and it feels like tenant concerns are constantly ignored. There’s little to no effort to actually cater to the needs of the people living here, which is the bare minimum you’d expect from any apartment complex.

That said, I do want to give credit where it’s due—Sheila, El Shadai, and Curtis have been consistently helpful, professional, and genuinely seem to care. They’ve made a frustrating experience slightly more bearable.

Unfortunately, not everyone meets that standard. Chez, in particular, has not been up to par and often contributes to the lack of effective communication and service.

Overall, the disconnect between management and tenants is very clear, and unless there are serious changes, I wouldn’t recommend living here.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Fatima Mahmoudi
text:
I moved out WEEKS ago and I’m STILL getting billed by this damn place. DO NOT MOVE HERE!!!!!

I was naive and young and needed a place to live. Nothing is worth this rent oh my god. You’re so much better off looking at Facebook marketplace, asking to rent a friend’s basement, or slumming it with your parents.

Firstly, the strangers you live with are abhorrent. My first interaction with my roommate upon moving in was abysmal and that set the tone for the entire time I lived there.

These stellar reviews are so disingenuous given the true atmosphere of this place. I hated every second of living here and leaped with such joy once I moved out.

Everyone is miserable. Every. One.

The smile on people’s faces leaves within the first week or two. Between the insane costs, crazy roommates, lack of management intervention, and “cleaning” crew, you have your hands full.

Do NOT, I repeat, move here. For your own sanity. I don’t know why they’re still charging me for nickels and dimes. Leave me alone.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Talyia Bradshaw
text:
I have lived at the apartment building for 2 years (since Aug 2023), across 2 different management companies. Disclaimer: everything below is alleged, on account to the experience and knowledge I have with this building. The original management company was not very helpful in regards to building needs I.e packages being stolen with no resolution from management, employees not being on site during working hours (often late), and upselling apartments by lying about Roomate selection.

The current management, Greystar, initially started off fine, the building manager was professional and the building held great events. However, over time the building became filled with corruption and cheap tactics.

- The products distributed in the shared resources were swapped was offbrand cheap items that are unusable (trash bags so thin they are see through)

- The app-controlled door locking system, Kastle takes so long to open and sometimes not at all. When multiple residents, including myself, asked for the devices to be fixed (charged or updated) the staffs response was that the app system was a luxury not a necessary, and they had no intention of making it right.

- Staff began to gossip on the private business of residents I.e. status of late rent, personal affairs, etc.

While there are obviously benefits to a co living building, the bs that comes with this place is not worth it. Do yourself a favor, choose one of the other 3 apartment in the area. And if you do still choose to live here, Dontreyl, a member of building staff, is very kind and will be your best bet to any sort of support on residential matters.

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Rebecca Austin
text:
I had such a great experience working with Dontreyl at Clover at The Parks. From the very beginning, he was incredibly kind, patient, and helpful. I had a lot of questions (and repeated a few more than once!), and he never once made me feel like I was asking too much. He answered every single one clearly and thoroughly, and always with professionalism and a genuinely friendly attitude.

What really stood out was how knowledgeable he was. He walked me through every detail—from pricing and availability to all the amenities, parking, utilities, and more. He even took the time out of his day to give me both a virtual and in-person tour, which made a huge difference for me. He made sure I was completely informed and comfortable every step of the way.

He also really took my budget and daily lifestyle into consideration, which I appreciated more than I can say. He helped me find the perfect unit that checked all the boxes without going over what I could afford. That kind of thoughtfulness and attention to detail is rare.

I honestly don’t think I could have gotten the apartment without how above and beyond Dontreyl went to help me. He made what could’ve been a stressful process feel smooth, and I’m truly grateful. Clover at The Parks is lucky to have him on the team, and I hope his manager sees just how valuable truly he is!

title: Clover at The Parks
name: Alex Elchev
text:
Common, as a company, does not care about its residents. This property is not unique in that sense. I've lived here for six months and my favorite part was moving out. You're lured in with "furnished" apartments (you get a mattress) and "cheap" rent (they raised my rent 15% since I started living there), and you're left with up to four roommates you've never met before who have absolutely no connection to you, nor a reason to care about you or the co-living situation.

First, don't get it twisted: your 1 bedroom is about 100 square feet, and the shared space is never used. Dishes will go missing and utensils will no longer be in the drawers. The kitchen will never get cleaned unless you do it. The trash will overflow and never get taken out unless you do it. I've asked support for more trash bags and an extra sponge for the kitchen I share with three other people, and they said to just split the cost amongst ourselves. If your whole selling point is that you get these materials and this support, where is it? I pay to live here, I'm not going to pay to clean up after strangers.

If you ask the property for any help at all, you will be outsourced (nothing against the support team, Jeffrey is great. This is all on Robert, the property manager). If you ask them, you won't even be able to contact your property manager, even when they TELL YOU TO CONTACT THE PROPERTY MANAGER. The building security is weak and I've had packages stolen with, you guessed it, absolutely no way to find  out who did it despite cameras all over the place.

Please, do yourself a favor, and seriously think twice about living here. You will be living in a dorm without an RA or any kind of admin. If you're planning on living here any time in the next six months (Jan - Jul 2024), there will also be LOTS of construction noise that starts promptly at 7am, six days a week. Not anyone's fault, but my tour guide did tell me that the noise was "minimal" on my tour.
